title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二 高帝下
title.en: Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 2
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二 高帝下 Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Gao of Southern Qi 2

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷第二 本紀第二

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 2, Annals 2
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 2, Annals 2

sentences.zh: 高帝下

translations.literal: Emperor Gao, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao (continued)

sentences.zh: 建元元年夏四月甲午，上卽皇帝位於南郊，設壇柴燎告天曰：「皇帝臣道成敢用玄牡，昭告皇皇后帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, fourth month, summer, day jiawu, the Emperor assumed the imperial throne at the Southern Altar, set up the altar, burned firewood offerings, and announced to Heaven: "The Emperor, your subject Daocheng, dares to use the black bull and announces to the August Sovereign above and the Empress below.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 1, summer, fourth month, day jiawu, he took the throne at the Southern Altar. The altar was raised, firewood was burned, and he addressed Heaven: "Your subject Daocheng, now Emperor, dares offer the black bull and declare to Heaven and Earth:

sentences.zh: 宋帝陟鑒乾序，欽若明命，以命于道成。

translations.literal: The Song Emperor has ascended to examine the sequence of Heaven, reverently followed the bright mandate, and bestowed the command upon Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor has read Heaven's order, bowed to the bright command, and entrusted the charge to Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 夫肇自生民，樹以司牧，所以闡極則天，開元創物，肆茲大道。

translations.literal: From the beginning of mankind rulers have been set up as shepherds, in order to reach the utmost and accord with Heaven, open the origin and create things, and spread this great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Since mankind began, rulers have been appointed to tend the folk, to touch the pole and mirror Heaven, to open an age and shape the world—to walk this great road.

sentences.zh: 天下惟公，命不于常。

translations.literal: Under Heaven only the public [virtue] [rules]; the mandate is not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The realm belongs to the worthy; the mandate does not stay with one house forever.

sentences.zh: 昔在虞、夏，受終上代，粵自漢、魏，揖讓中葉，咸炳諸典謨，載在方冊。

translations.literal: Formerly in Yu and Xia they received the end from the prior age; from Han and Wei onward, abdication in the middle ages—all shine in the canonical records and are written in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yu and Xia, the throne passed from the old line; from Han and Wei, rulers yielded in mid-dynasty—all of it glows in the classics and lives in the annals.

sentences.zh: 水德旣微，仍世多故，實賴道成匡拯之功，以弘濟于厥艱。

translations.literal: The Water phase has grown weak; generation after generation many troubles—truly relying on Daocheng's merit in righting and rescuing, to greatly cross through its hardships.
translations.idiomatic: The Water reign had faded and age after age brought disaster; only Daocheng's work of rescue bore the realm through its peril.

sentences.zh: 大造顛墜，再構區宇，宣禮明刑，締仁緝義。

translations.literal: Greatly repairing the fallen, reconstructing the realm, proclaiming rites and clarifying punishments, binding benevolence and gathering righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He raised what had collapsed, built the realm anew, set rites in the open and law in the light, and wove humanity and duty into the state.

sentences.zh: 晷緯凝象，川岳表靈，誕惟天人，罔弗和會。

translations.literal: The gnomon's lines fixed the images, rivers and mountains displayed their spirits; Heaven and man were born together—none failed to harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's shadow and the stars stood firm, rivers and peaks showed their numen; Heaven and humanity met, and all things fell into accord.

sentences.zh: 乃仰協歸運，景屬與能，用集大命于茲。

translations.literal: Thus bowing to accord with the returning fortune, the bright attribute attached to the able, thereby gathering the great mandate here.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to the turning of fate, the bright sign settled on worth, and the great charge was gathered here.

sentences.zh: 辭德匪嗣，至于累仍，而羣公卿士，庶尹御事，爰及黎獻，至于百戎，僉曰『皇天眷命，不可以固違，人神無托，不可以曠主』。

translations.literal: He declined virtue and would not succeed, even to repeated refusals; yet the host of ministers and grandees, the multitude of officials charged with affairs, down to the black-haired folk and the tribute-bearing border peoples, all said: "Imperial Heaven favors the mandate—it cannot be stubbornly disobeyed; men and spirits have nowhere to rest—it cannot be left without a lord."
translations.idiomatic: He refused the throne again and again, but ministers high and low, officers of every rank, the people, and the hundred border tribes cried as one: "Heaven has chosen—you cannot stand against it; gods and men need a lord—you cannot leave the throne empty."

sentences.zh: 畏天之威，敢不祗順鴻曆？

translations.literal: In awe of Heaven's majesty, how dare one not reverently follow the great calendar?
translations.idiomatic: Who, fearing Heaven's wrath, would not bow to the great succession?

sentences.zh: 敬簡元辰，虔奉皇符，升壇受禪，告類上帝，以永答民衷，式敷萬國。

translations.literal: Reverently choosing the first day, devoutly receiving the imperial tally, mounting the altar to receive abdication, announcing by category to the Supreme Lord, forever to answer the people's hearts and spread over the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: He chose the auspicious day, received the imperial tally in reverence, climbed the altar for the abdication rite, and reported to Heaven—to answer the people forever and bless the ten thousand realms.

sentences.zh: 惟明靈是饗！」

translations.literal: May the bright spirits partake!"
translations.idiomatic: May the bright powers accept this offering!"

sentences.zh: 禮畢，大駕還宮，臨太極前殿。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and attended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended, the imperial procession returned to the palace and took seat before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「五德更紹，帝迹所以代昌；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Five Phases succeed one another; thus imperial traces pass from house to house.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: "As the Five Phases turn, one throne gives way to the next.

sentences.zh: 三正迭隆，王度所以改耀。

translations.literal: The Three First Months rise in turn; thus royal measure changes its splendor.
translations.idiomatic: As the Three Calendars shift, the royal pattern takes a new light.

sentences.zh: 世有質文，時或因革，其資元膺曆，經道振民，固以異術同揆，殊流共貫者矣。

translations.literal: Ages have plainness and ornament, times now follow and now reform; those who bear the primal mandate, uphold the Way, and stir the people—surely they differ in method yet share one rule, diverge in stream yet run one course."
translations.idiomatic: Each age has its plain speech and its polish, and custom bends with the times; yet those who hold Heaven's first seal, keep the Way, and rouse the people—different tools, one measure; different currents, one channel."

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，屬值艱季，推肆勤之誠，藉樂治之數，賢能悉心，士民致力，用獲拯溺龕暴，一匡天下。

translations.literal: We, being shallow and dim, met a season of hardship; pushing forth the sincerity of diligence, relying on the reckoning of joyful rule, with worthies giving their hearts and gentry and people exerting their strength—we obtained rescue of the drowning and caging of the violent, and one correction of All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and small, and came to power in bitter years; by honest toil and the arts of good government, with the worthy giving all they had and the people lending their strength, we pulled the drowned from the flood, caged the cruel, and set the realm right in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 業未參古，功殆侔昔。

translations.literal: Our enterprise has not yet matched antiquity; our merit is nearly equal to the past.
translations.idiomatic: My work does not yet equal the ancients, yet my deed stands near theirs.

sentences.zh: 宋氏以陵夷有徵，歷數攸及，思弘樂推，永鑒崇替，爰集天祿于朕躬。

translations.literal: The Song house showed signs of decline; its term of years had arrived; thinking to extend the joy of yielding, forever to mirror elevation and fall, the celestial blessing was gathered upon Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Song was failing by every sign; its span had run its course. I wished only to honor the people's wish to yield, to read rise and fall in the mirror of history—and Heaven's blessing settled on me.

sentences.zh: 惟志菲薄，辭弗獲昭，遂欽從天人，式繇景命，祗月正于文祖，升禋鬯于上帝。

translations.literal: Our will is slight and thin; in declining we could not win clarity—thus we reverently followed Heaven and man, took the bright mandate as our path, reverently set the month at the Wen Ancestor, and ascended to offer fragrant spirits to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is humble; refusal brought no peace—so I bowed to Heaven and the people, followed the bright command, set the calendar month at the shrine of Wen, and offered the sacred ale to the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 猥以寡德，光宅四海，纂革代之蹤，托王公之上，若涉淵水，罔知所濟。

translations.literal: Unworthily, with slight virtue, we illuminate the four seas, continue the traces of the changing age, and rest above kings and dukes—like crossing deep water, not knowing what shore to reach.
translations.idiomatic: With little merit I now light the four seas, take up the trail of a new dynasty, and sit above kings and lords—as a man fording deep water who cannot see the far bank.

sentences.zh: 寶祚初啓，洪慶惟新，思俾利澤，宣被億兆，可大赦天下。

translations.literal: The precious throne is newly opened; great felicity is fresh—We think to extend benefit and grace, spread it over the hundred millions: a general amnesty is proclaimed for All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is new and blessing is renewed. I would let favor reach every corner of the realm: let there be a general amnesty throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 改昇明三年爲建元元年。

translations.literal: The third year of Shengming is changed to the first year of Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming 3 becomes Jianyuan 1.

sentences.zh: 賜民爵二級，文武進位二等，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者穀人五斛。

translations.literal: The people are granted two ranks of nobility; civil and military officers are advanced two grades; widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves are given five hu of grain each.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners receive two steps of rank; civil and military officers rise two grades; widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute alone receive five hu of grain apiece.

sentences.zh: 逋租宿債勿復收。

translations.literal: Overdue rents and old debts are not to be collected again.
translations.idiomatic: Back rent and old debts are forgiven.

sentences.zh: 有犯鄉論清議，贓汙淫盜，一皆蕩滌，洗除先注，與之更始。

translations.literal: Those guilty of village pure-criticism, corruption, lewdness, or theft—all are washed clean; prior notations are erased, and they are given a new beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses under village reputation law, graft, debauchery, and theft—all records are struck and names cleared for a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 長徒敕繫之囚，特皆原遣。

translations.literal: Long-term exiles and prisoners under edict are specially all pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Long-term convicts and those held by special order are pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 亡官失爵，禁錮奪勞，一依舊典。」

translations.literal: Those who lost office or rank, were confined or stripped of labor service—all according to the old statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Men who lost posts or titles, or who were barred or stripped of corvée—each case follows the former code."

sentences.zh: 封宋帝爲汝陰王，築宮丹陽縣故治，行宋正朔，車旗服色，一如故事，上書不爲表，答表不稱詔。

translations.literal: The Song Emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Runan; a palace was built at the old seat of Danyang county; Song calendar, chariot banners, and dress colors were all as before; when writing up he did not use the memorial form, and when replying to memorials the reply was not styled an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor became Prince of Runan, with a residence at old Danyang. He kept Song rites, banners, and colors. His letters were not called memorials; court replies to him were not called edicts.

sentences.zh: 降宋晉熙王燮爲陰安公，江夏王躋爲沙陽公，隨王翽爲舞陰公，新興王嵩爲定襄公，建安王禧爲荔浦公，郡公主爲縣君，縣公主爲鄉君。

translations.literal: Prince Jinxi of Song was reduced to Duke of Yin'an; Prince Jiangxia was made Duke of Shayang; Prince Sui was made Duke of Wuyin; Prince Xinxing was made Duke of Dingxiang; Prince Jian'an was made Duke of Lipu; princesses of commanderies became Ladies of counties; princesses of counties became Ladies of townships.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxi prince Xie became Duke of Yin'an; the Jiangxia, Sui, Xinxing, and Jian'an princes were demoted to county dukes; commandery princesses became county ladies, county princesses township ladies.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「繼世象賢，列代盛典，疇庸嗣美，前載令圖。

translations.literal: An edict said: "To succeed the line with the worthy is the constant ceremony of every age; to reward merit and continue beauty is the fine model of former records.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Passing the throne to the worthy is the rite of every dynasty; honoring merit and continuing a noble line is the pattern left by the ancients.

sentences.zh: 宋氏通侯，乃宜隨運省替。

translations.literal: The marquises and earls of the Song house should indeed follow the turn of fortune and be reduced or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Song's feudal ranks should shrink with the change of house.

sentences.zh: 但欽德懷義，尚表墳閭，況功濟區夏，道光民俗者哉？

translations.literal: Yet those who revered virtue and cherished righteousness still had their tombs honored—how much more those whose merit saved the realm and whose light guided the folk?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet men who loved righteousness still had their graves tended—what of those whose work saved the realm and whose fame lit the people?"

sentences.zh: 降差之典，宜遵往制。

translations.literal: The statutes of reduction should follow former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The rules of demotion should follow the old precedents.

sentences.zh: 南康縣公華容縣公可爲侯，萍鄉縣侯可爲伯，減戶有差，以繼劉穆之、王弘、何無忌後。」

translations.literal: The County Duke of Nankang and the County Duke of Huarong may become marquises; the Marquis of Pingxiang may become an earl; household quotas are reduced by grade, to continue the lines of Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong, and He Wuji."
translations.idiomatic: The county dukes of Nankang and Huarong are made marquises; the marquis of Pingxiang is made an earl; household quotas are cut by rank, to carry on the houses of Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong, and He Wuji."

sentences.zh: 以司空褚淵爲司徒，吳郡太守柳世隆爲南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Grand Minister; Administrator of Wu Commandery Liu Shilong was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, minister of works, became grand minister; Liu Shilong, administrator of Wu, became inspector of South Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「宸運肇創，實命惟新，宜弘慶宥，廣敷蠲汰。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The imperial fortune is newly founded; the mandate is fresh—felicity and pardon should be broadly spread, and exemptions widely granted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The throne is new and the charge is new—let mercy run wide and burdens be lifted.

sentences.zh: 劫賊餘口沒在臺府者，悉原放。

translations.literal: Surviving captives of bandit raids held in the palace offices are all pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Captives left from rebel raids and held in central offices are all freed.

sentences.zh: 諸負釁流徙，普聽還本土。

translations.literal: All who bear guilt and were exiled or banished may generally hear that they may return to their native lands."
translations.idiomatic: Exiles and banished men may return home."

sentences.zh: 」以齊國左衛將軍陳顯達爲中護軍，中領軍王敬則爲南兖州刺史，左衛將軍李安民爲中領軍。

translations.literal: Left Guards General of Qi State Chen Xianda was made Director of the Central Guard; Central Army Commander Wang Jingze was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; Left Guards General Li Anmin was made Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda, left guards general of Qi, became director of the central guard; Wang Jingze, central army commander, inspector of South Yanzhou; Li Anmin, left guards general, central army commander.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以荊州刺史嶷爲尚書令、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，冠軍將軍映爲荊州刺史，西中郎將晃爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍垣崇祖爲豫州刺史，驃騎司馬崔文仲爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, Inspector of Jing Province Luan was made Director of the Master of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might, with Grand Secretariat and staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Yang Province; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Ying was made Inspector of Jing Province; West General of the Gentlemen Huang was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Yuan Chongzu was made Inspector of Yu Province; Chief Commandant of the General Who Spreads Might Cui Wenzong was made Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Day wuxu: Luan, inspector of Jing, became director of the master of writing, general-in-chief who spreads might, with secretariat equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Yang; Ying, champion general, inspector of Jing; Huang, west general of the gentlemen, inspector of South Xuzhou; Yuan Chongzu, champion general, inspector of Yu; Cui Wenzong, chief commandant under the general who spreads might, inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 斷四方上慶禮。

translations.literal: Congratulatory rites from the four quarters were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrations sent in from the provinces were halted.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔曰：「自廬井毀制，農桑易業，鹽鐵妨民，貨鬻傷治，歷代成俗，流蠹歲滋。

translations.literal: On day jihai an edict said: "Since lanes and wells were ruined and farming and mulberry changed trade, salt and iron have harmed the people and market sales have injured good order—custom of successive ages, a running sore year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Day jihai: an edict said: "Since fields and hamlets fell into ruin and farmers turned to trade, salt monopolies and iron dues have hurt the people and peddling has poisoned government—an old evil that grows worse each year.

sentences.zh: 援拯遺弊，革末反本，使公不專利，氓無失業。

translations.literal: To rescue the lingering ill and return the branch to the root, so that the public does not monopolize profit and the folk do not lose their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: We must heal what remains and turn the realm back to its root, so lords do not hoard gain and the people do not lose their work.

sentences.zh: 二宮諸王，悉不得營立屯邸，封略山湖。

translations.literal: The two palaces and all princes are altogether forbidden to establish estate manors or seize mountain lakes."
translations.idiomatic: Neither inner palace nor princes may build manor estates or fence off mountains and lakes."

sentences.zh: 太官池籞，宮停稅入，優量省置。

translations.literal: The palace ponds and preserves, and taxes on palace lands, are to be favorably gauged and offices reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial fishponds and parks, and levies on palace lands, are to be trimmed and posts cut.

sentences.zh: 」庚子，詔「宋帝后蕃王諸陵，宜有守衛。

translations.literal: On day gengzi an edict: "The tombs of the Song emperor, empresses, princes, and princesses should have guards."
translations.idiomatic: Day gengzi: "The tombs of the Song house—emperor, consorts, princes, and princesses—shall have guards."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏帝陵各置長一人，兵有差，王陵五人，妃嬪三人。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that each imperial tomb should have one chief warden and soldiers in set numbers: five for princely tombs, three for consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries proposed one tomb chief per imperial mound, with fixed guards: five men for princes' tombs, three for consorts'.

sentences.zh: 五月丙午，進河南王吐谷渾拾寅號驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day bingwu: Prince Murong Shibin of Henan was advanced to General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day bingwu: Murong Shibin of Henan was promoted to general-in-chief who spreads might.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「宸運革命，引爵改封，宋氏第秩，雖宜省替，其有預效屯夷、宣力齊業者，一仍本封，無所減降。

translations.literal: An edict said: "With the imperial fortune revolutionized, ranks and fiefs are changed; Song titles should indeed be reduced with the times—yet those who early showed merit on the frontiers or labored for Qi's founding shall keep their original fiefs without reduction."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The dynasty has turned; titles must be refitted. Song ranks should shrink—but men who proved themselves on the border or helped found Qi keep their old fiefs whole."

sentences.zh: 有司奏留襄陽郡公張敬兒等六十二人，除廣興郡公沈曇亮等百二十二人。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that sixty-two men including Zhang Jing'er, Marquis of Xiangyang, were retained; one hundred twenty-two men including Shen Tanliang, Duke of Guangxing, were removed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries listed sixty-two men, including Zhang Jing'er of Xiangyang, whose titles stood; one hundred twenty-two, including Shen Tanliang of Guangxing, were struck.

sentences.zh: 改《元嘉曆》爲《建元曆》，木德盛卯終未，以正月卯祖，十二月未臘。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia Calendar was changed to the Jianyuan Calendar; the Wood phase flourished from mao through wei; the first month took mao as ancestor, the twelfth month had wei as year-end sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia calendar became the Jianyuan calendar. Wood ruled from mao to wei; the year opened in mao and closed with the wei sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「設募取將，懸賞購士，蓋出權宜，非曰恆制。

translations.literal: On day dingwei an edict said: "Setting rewards to take generals and posting bounties to buy warriors are measures of expediency, not the constant system.
translations.idiomatic: Day dingwei: an edict said: "Bounty lists for captains and price tags for soldiers are expedients, not permanent law.

sentences.zh: 頃世艱險，浸以成俗，且長逋逸，開罪山湖。

translations.literal: In recent generations hardship has deepened until it became custom, and long flight opened the mountains and lakes to crime.
translations.idiomatic: Hard times made the practice common; men fled for years and crime hid in the hills.

sentences.zh: 是爲黥刑不辱，亡竄無咎。

translations.literal: Thus tattoo punishment did not shame them, and flight brought no blame.
translations.idiomatic: Branding no longer shamed them; outlaw life carried no stain.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，可斷衆募。

translations.literal: From this time forward, mass recruitment may be ended."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, open recruiting is forbidden."

sentences.zh: 」壬子，詔封佐命文武功臣新除司徒褚淵等三十一人，進爵增戶各有差。

translations.literal: On day renzi an edict enfeoffed thirty-one men including the newly appointed Grand Minister Chu Yuan, meritorious civil and military ministers who aided the founding, with advancement of rank and increase of households each according to grade.
translations.idiomatic: Day renzi: thirty-one founding ministers, including the new grand minister Chu Yuan, were enfeoffed; rank and household quotas rose by merit.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，河南王吐谷渾拾寅奉表貢獻。

translations.literal: On day yimao Prince Murong Shibin of Henan presented a memorial with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Day yimao: Murong Shibin of Henan sent tribute with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔遣大使分行四方，遣兼散騎常侍十二人巡行。

translations.literal: On day bingchen an edict sent great envoys to tour the four quarters, dispatching twelve men as concurrent Regular Attendants of Scattered Cavalry to make the rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingchen: great envoys were sent on circuit through the realm, twelve of them bearing the concurrent title of regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以交寧道遠，不遣使。

translations.literal: Because Jiao and Ning were far, no envoys were sent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao and Ning were too distant; no envoys went there.

sentences.zh: 己未，汝陰王薨，追諡爲宋順帝，終禮依魏元、晉恭帝故事。

translations.literal: On day jiwei the Prince of Runan died; he was posthumously titled Emperor Shun of Song; final rites followed the precedents of Emperor Yuan of Wei and Emperor Gong of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiwei: the Prince of Runan died and was posthumously styled Emperor Shun of Song; his funeral followed Wei's Emperor Yuan and Jin's Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，陰安公劉燮等伏誅。

translations.literal: On day xinyou Liu Xie, Duke of Yin'an, and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinyou: Liu Xie, Duke of Yin'an, and his party were put to death.

sentences.zh: 追封諡上兄道度爲衡陽元王，道生爲始安貞王。

translations.literal: Posthumous enfeoffment was granted: the Emperor's elder brother Daodu was titled Prince Yuan of Hengyang; Daosheng was titled Prince Zhen of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: The elder brothers were honored after death: Daodu as Prince Yuan of Hengyang, Daosheng as Prince Zhen of Shian.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，追尊皇考曰宣皇帝，皇妣爲孝皇后，妃爲昭皇后。

translations.literal: On day bingyin the Imperial Father was posthumously honored as Emperor Xuan; the Imperial Mother as Empress Xiao; the consort as Empress Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingyin: the imperial father was styled Emperor Xuan, the imperial mother Empress Xiao, the consort Empress Zhao.

sentences.zh: 六月辛未，詔「相國驃騎中軍三府職，可依資勞度二官，若職限已盈，所餘可賜滿。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day xinwei: an edict—"Posts in the Three Offices of the Chancellor, the General Who Spreads Might, and the Central Army may be filled according to merit and seniority with two officers each; if the quota is full, the remainder may be granted to full salary."
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day xinwei: "Offices of the chancellery, the general who spreads might, and the central army may each take two men by merit and tenure; any posts beyond quota may be paid at full rate."

sentences.zh: 」壬申，以遊擊將軍周山圖爲兖州刺史。

translations.literal: On day renshen Mobile Corps General Zhou Shantu was made Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Day renshen: Zhou Shantu, mobile corps general, became inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「宋末頻年戎寇，兼災疾凋損，或枯骸不收，毀櫬莫掩，宜速宣下埋藏營䘏。

translations.literal: On day yihai an edict said: "In the last years of Song, year after year brought raids and plague; some dead were left unburied, some coffins destroyed and never covered—burial and mourning arrangements should be quickly announced."
translations.idiomatic: Day yihai: "Song's last years saw war and pestilence. Bones lay in the open; broken coffins went uncovered. Let burial and mourning be ordered at once."

sentences.zh: 若標題猶存，姓字可識，可卽運載，致還本鄉。

translations.literal: If markers still remain and surnames can be read, they should at once be transported and returned to their native districts."
translations.idiomatic: Where tags survive and names can be read, the dead are to be carried home."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏遣外監典事四人，周行離門外三十五里爲限。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized dispatch of four overseers from the outer office, ranging thirty-five li beyond the outer gates as their limit.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries sent four overseers from the outer bureau, each to work within thirty-five li of the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 其餘班下州郡。

translations.literal: The rest were ordered down to the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Other regions were handled by the provinces and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 無棺器標題者，屬所以臺錢供市。

translations.literal: Where there were no coffins or markers, the local office was to supply them from central funds.
translations.idiomatic: Where there was no coffin or name marker, local officials were to buy them with funds from the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，七廟主備法駕卽于太廟。

translations.literal: On day gengchen the seven ancestral tablets, with the full imperial equipage, were escorted to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Day gengchen: the seven temple tablets, with full imperial escort, entered the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 詔「諸將及客，戮力艱難，盡勤直衛，其從還宮者，普賜位一階。

translations.literal: An edict: "All generals and retainers who strove through hardship and gave loyal service in the guard—those who returned to the palace with Us are generally granted one step of rank."
translations.idiomatic: "Every officer and client who fought through the hard years and kept faithful guard—those who came home with me receive one step of rank."

sentences.zh: 」辛巳，罷荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On day xinsi the office of Inspector of Jing Province was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinsi: the post of inspector of Jing was abolished.

sentences.zh: 甲申，立皇太子賾。

translations.literal: On day jiashen the Heir Apparent Ze was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiashen: the heir apparent Ze was formally named.

sentences.zh: 斷諸州郡禮慶。

translations.literal: Congratulatory rites from all provinces and commanderies were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrations from the provinces were stopped.

sentences.zh: 見刑入重者，降一等，幷申前赦恩百日。

translations.literal: Those who entered with serious punishment had their sentence reduced one grade, and the prior amnesty grace was extended by one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts under heavy sentence were lowered one degree, and the earlier pardon was extended by a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 立皇子嶷爲豫章王，映爲臨川王，晃爲長沙王，曅爲武陵王，暠爲安成王，鏘爲鄱陽王，鑠爲桂陽王，鑒爲廣陵王，皇孫長懋爲南郡王。

translations.literal: The princes Luan was made Prince of Yuzhang; Ying Prince of Linchuan; Huang Prince of Changsha; Ye Prince of Wuling; Gao Prince of Ancheng; Qiang Prince of Poyang; Shuo Prince of Guiyang; Jian Prince of Guangling; the imperial grandson Zhangmao Prince of Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were named: Luan of Yuzhang, Ying of Linchuan, Huang of Changsha, Ye of Wuling, Gao of Ancheng, Qiang of Poyang, Shuo of Guiyang, Jian of Guangling; the imperial grandson Zhangmao became prince of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，葬宋順帝于遂寧陵。

translations.literal: On day yiyou Emperor Shun of Song was buried at Suining Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Day yiyou: Emperor Shun of Song was laid in Suining tomb.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁未，詔曰：「交阯比景，獨隔書朔，斯乃前運方季，負海不朝，因迷遂往，歸款莫由。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingwei: an edict said: "Jiaozhi and Biying stand alone beyond our written calendar—this is the late fortune of a former age, facing the sea yet not coming to court; lost in error they went on, and there was no road back to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, day dingwei: an edict said: "Jiaozhi and Biying lie beyond our maps and calendars—remnants of a failing age, facing the sea yet never bowing; they wandered in error with no way home.

sentences.zh: 曲赦交州部內李叔獻一人卽撫南士，文武詳才選用。

translations.literal: A special pardon is granted within Jiao Province to Li Shuxian alone, that he may pacify the southern lands; civil and military talent is to be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao province receives a special pardon for Li Shuxian alone, that he may settle the south; worthy civil and military men are to be chosen carefully.

sentences.zh: 幷遣大使宣揚朝恩。

translations.literal: Great envoys are also sent to proclaim the court's grace."
translations.idiomatic: Great envoys will carry the throne's mercy abroad."

sentences.zh: 」以試守武平太守行交州府事李叔獻爲交州刺史。

translations.literal: Acting Administrator of Wuping, holding the office of Jiao Province, Li Shuxian was made Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuxian, acting administrator of Wuping and acting for Jiao province, became inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以虜偽茄蘆鎮主陰平公楊廣香爲沙州刺史。

translations.literal: On day bingchen Yang Guangxiang, Duke of Yinping, lord of the enemy fort Qielu, was made Inspector of Sha Province.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingchen: Yang Guangxiang of Yinping, lord of the barbarian fort Qielu, became inspector of Sha.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔「南蘭陵桑梓本鄉，長蠲租布；

translations.literal: On day dingsi an edict: "Southern Lanling, native district of the imperial clan, is permanently exempt from land tax and cloth levy;
translations.idiomatic: Day dingsi: "Southern Lanling, the clan's home, is forever free of grain rent and cloth tax;

sentences.zh: 武進王業所基，復十年。」

translations.literal: Wujin, base of the royal house's enterprise, is exempt for ten years."
translations.idiomatic: Wujin, where the house first rose, is exempt for ten years."

sentences.zh: 九月辛丑，詔「二吳、義興三郡遭水，減今年田租。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day xinchou: an edict—"The two Wu commanderies and Yixing—three circuits—suffered flood; this year's field tax is reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, day xinchou: "The two Wu districts and Yixing, all three struck by flood, pay reduced field tax this year."

sentences.zh: 」乙巳，以新除尚書令、驃騎將軍豫章王嶷爲荊、湘二州刺史，平西將軍臨川王映爲揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On day yisi the newly appointed Director of the Master of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might, Prince of Yuzhang Luan was made Inspector of Jing and Xiang; General Who Pacifies the West, Prince of Linchuan Ying was made Inspector of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Day yisi: Luan, new director of the master of writing and general who spreads might, prince of Yuzhang, took Jing and Xiang; Ying, prince of Linchuan and general who pacifies the west, took Yang.

sentences.zh: 丙午，司空褚淵領尚書令。

translations.literal: On day bingwu Minister of Works Chu Yuan also held the office of Director of the Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Day bingwu: Chu Yuan, minister of works, also directed the master of writing.

sentences.zh: 戊申，車駕幸宣武堂宴會，詔諸王公以下賦詩。

translations.literal: On day wushen the imperial carriage visited the Xuanwu Hall for a banquet; an edict ordered all princes and dukes downward to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: Day wushen: the emperor feasted at Xuanwu Hall and ordered every prince and noble down the line to write a poem.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚子，以太子左衛率蕭景先爲司州刺史。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengzi: Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard Xiao Jingxian was made Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, day gengzi: Xiao Jingxian, left commandant of the heir's guard, became inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，立皇太子妃裴氏。

translations.literal: On day xinhai the Heir Apparent's consort, Lady Pei, was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinhai: Lady Pei was installed as heir's consort.

sentences.zh: 甲申，封功臣驃騎長史江謐等十人爵戶各有差。

translations.literal: On day jiashen meritorious ministers including Chief Commandant of the General Who Spreads Might Jiang Mi were enfeoffed with ranks and households each according to grade.
translations.idiomatic: Day jiashen: ten meritorious ministers, including Jiang Mi, chief commandant under the general who spreads might, received fiefs and household quotas by merit.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月戊戌朔，大赦天下。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, first month, day wuxu, first day of the month: a general amnesty for All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Year 2, spring, first month, new year's day: general amnesty for the realm.

sentences.zh: 以司空、尚書令褚淵爲司徒，中軍將軍張敬兒爲車騎將軍，中領軍李安民爲領軍將軍，中護軍陳顯達爲護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Director of the Master of Writing Chu Yuan was made Grand Minister; Central Army Commander Zhang Jing'er was made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Central Army Commander Li Anmin was made Director of the Central Army; Director of the Central Guard Chen Xianda was made Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, minister of works and director of the master of writing, became grand minister; Zhang Jing'er, central army commander, general of chariots and cavalry; Li Anmin, central army commander, director of the central army; Chen Xianda, director of the central guard, director of the guard.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，車駕親祠南郊。

translations.literal: On day xinchou the imperial carriage in person sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: Day xinchou: the emperor offered sacrifice at the Southern Altar in person.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔索虜寇淮、泗，遣衆軍北伐，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: On day guimao an edict: the northern enemy raided Huai and Si; hosts were sent on a northern campaign, and within and without the court martial law was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Day guimao: an edict—northern raiders struck Huai and Si; armies marched north and the court and camps alike went on war footing.

sentences.zh: 二月丁卯，虜寇壽陽，豫州刺史垣崇祖破走之。

translations.literal: In the second month, day dingmao, the barbarians raided Shouyang; Inspector of Yuzhou Yuan Chonggu defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day dingmao: the northerners struck Shouyang; Yuan Chonggu, inspector of Yuzhou, broke them and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 置巴州。

translations.literal: Ba province was established.
translations.idiomatic: The court established Ba province.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以三巴校尉明慧昭爲巴州刺史。

translations.literal: On day renshen, Colonel of the Three Ba Ming Huizhao was made Inspector of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: On day renshen, Ming Huizhao, colonel of the Three Ba, was appointed inspector of Ba.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以寧蠻校尉蕭赤斧爲雍州刺史，南蠻長史崔惠景爲梁、南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Colonel Who Pacifies the Man Xiao Chifu was made Inspector of Yongzhou; Chief Clerk for the Southern Man Cui Huijing was made Inspector of Liang and South Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuzi, Xiao Chifu, colonel who pacifies the Man, took Yongzhou; Cui Huijing, chief clerk for the southern Man, took Liang and South Qin.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔西境獻捷，解嚴。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, an edict: reports of victory from the western frontier—martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinmao an edict announced western victories and stood the realm down from martial alert.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，遣大使巡慰淮、肥。

translations.literal: On day guisi, grand envoys were sent to tour and comfort the Huai and Fei.
translations.idiomatic: On day guisi the court dispatched grand envoys to tour and comfort the Huai and Fei regions.

sentences.zh: 徐、豫邊民尤貧遘難者，刺史二千石量加賑恤。

translations.literal: Among the border people of Xu and Yu who were especially poor and had suffered hardship, the inspectors and the two-thousand-bushel officials were to grant relief according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors and prefects along the Xu and Yu frontier were to measure out extra relief for those worst hit by poverty and war.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔「江西北民避難流徙者，制遣還本，蠲今年租稅。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, an edict: "People north and west of the river who fled hardship and drifted away—regulations send them back to their native places and remit this year's land tax and levies.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiawu an edict ran: "Refugees from north and west of the Yangtze are to be sent home under the standing rules, and this year's land tax is forgiven.

sentences.zh: 單貧及孤老不能自存者，卽聽番籍，郡縣押領。」

translations.literal: Those alone, destitute, orphaned, or aged who cannot support themselves may at once be entered on local registers; the commanderies and counties shall escort and settle them."
translations.idiomatic: The solitary poor, orphans, and aged who cannot live by themselves may be registered where they are; counties and commanderies shall take charge and see them settled."

sentences.zh: 三月丁酉，以侍中西昌侯鸞爲郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, day dingyou, Palace Attendant, Marquis of Xichang Luan was made Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day dingyou: Palace Attendant Luan, Marquis of Xichang, was made inspector of Ying.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以護軍將軍陳顯達爲南兖州刺史，吳郡太守張岱爲中護軍。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, Protector of the Army Chen Xianda was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; Administrator of Wu Commandery Zhang Dai was made Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuxu, Chen Xianda, protector of the army, took South Yanzhou; Zhang Dai, administrator of Wu, became central protector of the army.

sentences.zh: 己亥，車駕幸樂游苑宴，王公以下賦詩。

translations.literal: On day jihai, the imperial carriage visited the Pleasure Gardens for a banquet; princes, dukes, and officials down to the lowest ranks were ordered to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai the emperor feasted at the Pleasure Gardens and commanded every lord and officer present to offer a poem.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以征虜將軍崔祖思爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: On day xinchou, General Who Punishes the Barbarians Cui Zusi was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinchou, Cui Zusi, general who punishes the barbarians, was given Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙寅，進高麗王樂浪公高璉號驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, day bingyin, King of Koguryo, Marquis of Lelang Gao Lian was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, day bingyin: Gao Lian, king of Koguryo and marquis of Lelang, was promoted to general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 五月，立六門都牆。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the outer walls of the six gates were raised.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the six city gates were given new outer walls.

sentences.zh: 六月癸未，詔「昔歲水旱，曲赦丹陽、二吳、義興四郡遭水尤劇之縣，元年以前，三調未充，虛列已畢，官長局吏應共償備外，詳所除宥。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month, day guiwei, an edict: "In past years flood and drought struck; a special amnesty is granted to the four commanderies of Danyang, the two Wu, and Yixing for those districts worst afflicted by water. For the three levies left unpaid before the first year of Jianyuan, though the books show them cleared, the clerks and bureau officers who should jointly make good the shortfall are, beyond that, to have the remission set out in detail."
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day guiwei: an edict said that after years of flood and drought, Danyang, the two Wu, and Yixing—where the damage was worst—should receive a targeted pardon; unpaid triple levies before Jianyuan 1, though already written off on the registers, would not be chased from the clerks except as the edict spelled out.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲寅，以輔國將軍盧紹之爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, day jiayin, Assistant General Lu Shaozhi was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, day jiayin: Lu Shaozhi, assistant general, was made inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 戊午，皇太子妃裴氏薨。

translations.literal: On day wuwu the crown prince's consort, Lady Pei, died.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuwu the crown prince's consort, Lady Pei, died.

sentences.zh: 閏月辛巳，遣領軍將軍李安民行淮、泗。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, day xinsi, Colonel Director of the Army Li Anmin was sent to tour the Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, day xinsi: Li Anmin, colonel director of the army, was sent to tour the Huai and Si.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，索虜攻朐山，青、冀二州刺史盧紹之等破走之。

translations.literal: On day gengyin the northern barbarians attacked Qushan; Lu Shaozhi and others, inspectors of Qing and Ji, defeated and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengyin the northerners attacked Qushan; Lu Shaozhi of Qing and Ji broke them and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月戊子，以氐楊後起爲秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, day wuzi, the Di chieftain Yang Houqi was made Inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, eleventh month, day wuzi: Yang Houqi of the Di was made inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，以司空褚淵爲司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, day wuxu, Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, day wuxu: Chu Yuan moved from minister of works to minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，車駕幸中堂聽訟。

translations.literal: On day yisi the imperial carriage visited the Central Hall to hear lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: On day yisi the emperor heard cases in the Central Hall.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以驃騎大將軍豫章王嶷爲司空，揚州刺史、前將軍臨川王映爲荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On day renzi, General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan was made Minister of Works; Inspector of Yangzhou, Forward General, Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying was made Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On day renzi, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan, general of agile cavalry, became minister of works; Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying, forward general and inspector of Yangzhou, took Jing.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月壬戌朔，詔王公卿士薦讜言。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year, day renxu, first day of the month, an edict called on princes, dukes, ministers, and scholars to recommend forthright words.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, third year, first month, day renxu, new moon: the court asked lords and ministers to submit candid counsel.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以平北將軍陳顯達爲益州刺史，貞陽公柳世隆爲南兖州刺史，皇子鋒爲江夏王。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, Pacifying North General Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Yi; Duke of Zhenyang Liu Shilong was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; the imperial son Feng was made Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingzi, Chen Xianda, pacifying north, took Yi; Liu Shilong, duke of Zhenyang, took South Yanzhou; the prince Feng was enfeoffed as prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍李安民等破虜于淮陽。

translations.literal: Colonel Director of the Army Li Anmin and others defeated the barbarians at Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anmin, colonel director of the army, and his colleagues routed the barbarians at Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，以寧朔將軍沈景德爲廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Pacifying the North General Shen Jingde was made Inspector of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month: Shen Jingde, pacifying the north, was made inspector of Guang.

sentences.zh: 六月壬子，大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, day renzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, day renzi: a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 逋租宿債，除減有差。

translations.literal: Overdue rent and old debts were remitted in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: Overdue rents and old debts were forgiven in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，以冠軍將軍垣榮祖爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Champion General Yuan Rongzu was made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month: Yuan Rongzu, champion general, took Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊子，以河南王世子吐谷渾易度侯爲西秦、河二州刺史，河南王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, day wuzi, the heir of the King of Henan, Tuyuhun Yidu Hou, was made Inspector of West Qin and He, and King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, tenth month, day wuzi: Yidu Hou of the Tuyuhun, heir of the king of Henan, was made inspector of West Qin and He and confirmed as king of Henan.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月壬戌，詔曰：「夫膠庠之典，彝倫攸先，所以招振才端，啓發性緒，弘字黎氓，納之軌義，是故五禮之迹可傳，六樂之容不泯。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fourth year, day renxu, an edict said: "The institution of the school and academy is the constant that human relations hold first, the means to summon and shake out talent, to open one's nature and bent, to enlarge and settle the black-haired people, and to take them into the track of right—thus the traces of the five rites can be handed down and the countenance of the six joys does not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, fourth year, first month, day renxu: an edict declared that the academy is the first pillar of human order—the place to gather talent, wake inclination, settle the people, and set them on the path of ritual, so that the five rites may endure and the six joys not fade.

sentences.zh: 朕自膺曆受圖，志闡經訓，且有司羣僚，奏議咸集，蓋以戎車時警，文教未宣，思樂泮宮，永言多慨。

translations.literal: Since I received the chart and mandate, my aim has been to clarify the classics and instructions, and the responsible offices and assembled ministers have all submitted plans together—yet with war-chariots ever on alert, culture and teaching have not been spread abroad; I think longingly of the Pan pool and sigh again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne I have meant to revive the canon, and the ministries have piled up proposals—yet with armies always under arms, learning has gone unproclaimed, and I long for the schools with mounting regret.

sentences.zh: 今關燧無虞，時和歲稔，遠邇同風，華夷慕義。

translations.literal: Now the beacon-fires are quiet, the seasons harmonious and the harvest rich; far and near share one wind, and Chinese and barbarian alike incline to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Now the frontier is still, the year is kind, and near and far, Han and barbarian, turn toward the court.

sentences.zh: 便可式遵前准，修建敩學，精選儒官，廣延國胄。

translations.literal: Let us at once follow the former standard, repair and build the school of instruction, carefully select Confucian officers, and broadly enroll the sons of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Let the old model be followed: rebuild the imperial school, choose true scholars for its offices, and enroll the sons of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」以江州刺史王延之爲右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Wang Yanzhi was made Senior Master of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhi, inspector of Jiangzhou, was made senior master of the bright hall.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「比歲申威西北，義勇爭先，殞氣寇場，命盡王事。

translations.literal: On day guihai, an edict said: "In recent years we showed might in the northwest; volunteers vied to be first, and men gave their breath on the battlefield and their lives for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On day guihai an edict said: "These last years in the northwest our soldiers strove to outdo one another; many fell in battle for the throne.

sentences.zh: 戰亡蠲復，雖有恆典，主者遵用，每傷簡薄。

translations.literal: Exemption for the fallen in war has a standing rule, but those in charge, in applying it, have often made it too spare.
translations.idiomatic: The usual exemptions for the war dead exist, but officials have applied them grudgingly.

sentences.zh: 建元以來戰亡，賞蠲租布二十年，雜役十年。

translations.literal: For those who died in battle since Jianyuan, reward and exemption from rent and cloth for twenty years, and from miscellaneous corvée for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: All who have died in battle since Jianyuan shall have twenty years' remission of rent and cloth and ten years' remission of labor.

sentences.zh: 其不得收屍，主軍保押，亦同此例。

translations.literal: Where the body could not be recovered, the commanding officer shall stand surety—the same rule applies.
translations.idiomatic: Where no body could be brought home, the field commander shall stand guarantor under the same terms.

sentences.zh: 」以後將軍長沙王晃爲護軍將軍，中軍將軍南郡王長懋爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍安成王暠爲江州刺史。

translations.literal: " Rear General, Prince of Changsha Xiao Huang was made Protector of the Army; General of the Center, Prince of Nan Commandery Xiao Changmao was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; Champion General, Prince of Ancheng Xiao Hao was made Inspector of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince of Changsha Xiao Huang, rear general, became protector of the army; Prince of Nan Commandery Xiao Changmao, general of the center, took South Xuzhou; Prince of Ancheng Xiao Hao, champion general, took Jiang.

sentences.zh: 二月乙未，以冠軍將軍桓康爲青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, day yiwei, Champion General Huan Kang was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, day yiwei: Huan Kang, champion general, was given Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 上不豫，庚戌，詔原京師囚繫有差，元年以前逋責皆原除。

translations.literal: The emperor fell ill; on day gengxu an edict pardoned capital prisoners in graded fashion and remitted all overdue obligations before the first year of Jianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell ill. On day gengxu an edict freed capital prisoners by degrees and wiped out all arrears before Jianyuan 1.

sentences.zh: 三月庚申，召司徒褚淵、左僕射王儉詔曰：「吾本布衣素族，念不到此，因藉時來，遂隆大業。

translations.literal: In the third month, day gengshen, Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan and Left Vice Director of the Master of Writing Wang Jian were summoned; the edict said: "I was originally of a plain cloth clan and never thought to reach this; relying on the times, I have at last ascended the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, day gengshen: Chu Yuan, minister over the masses, and Wang Jian, left vice director of the master of writing, were called in. The edict said: "I began as a man of plain cloth and never dreamed of this height; the age lifted me, and so I came to the throne.

sentences.zh: 風道沾被，升平可期。

translations.literal: The wind of the Way has soaked through; peace and order may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: The Way has begun to soak the realm; peace may yet be hoped for.

sentences.zh: 遘疾彌留，至于大漸。

translations.literal: I have met illness that lingers and now approach the great passing.
translations.idiomatic: Sickness holds me fast, and the great passing is near.

sentences.zh: 公等奉太子如事吾，柔遠能邇，緝和內外，當令太子敦穆親戚，委任賢才，崇尚節儉，弘宣簡惠，則天下之理盡矣。

translations.literal: You are to serve the crown prince as you served me: gentle with the distant, able with the near, harmonizing within and without. See that the crown prince treats his kin with generous courtesy, entrusts the worthy, honors frugality, and spreads simplicity and grace—then the principle of All-under-Heaven will be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the crown prince as you have served me: be gentle to the far and firm with the near, knit court and country together. Let him cherish his kin, employ the worthy, love thrift, and show a simple kindness—and the realm will be well ordered.

sentences.zh: 死生有命，夫復何言！

translations.literal: Life and death have their mandate—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are Heaven's order—what more can I say!"

sentences.zh: 」壬戌，上崩于臨光殿，年五十六。

translations.literal: On day renxu the emperor died in the Hall of Facing the Light, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: On day renxu the emperor died in the Hall of Facing the Light, at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 四月庚寅，上諡曰太祖高皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, day gengyin, the posthumous title was announced: Grand Progenitor, High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, day gengyin: he was given the temple title Grand Progenitor, High Emperor.

sentences.zh: 奉梓宮於東府前渚升龍舟。

translations.literal: The coffin was borne to the dragon boat at the ford before the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin was carried to the dragon boat at the ford before the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙午，窆武進泰安陵。

translations.literal: On day bingwu he was buried at Tai'an Mausoleum in Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingwu he was buried at Tai'an Mausoleum in Wujin.

sentences.zh: 上少沈深有大量，寬嚴清儉，喜怒無色。

translations.literal: In youth the emperor was deep and reserved, with great capacity; strict yet generous, pure and frugal; joy and anger never showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was deep and still, with a large soul: stern when needed, open-handed, pure and spare; neither joy nor anger showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 博涉經史，善屬文，工草隸書，弈棊第二品。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through the classics and histories, was skilled at literary composition, practiced clerical and cursive script, and at go ranked second class.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories, wrote well, practiced clerical and cursive script, and at go held second rank.

sentences.zh: 雖經綸夷險，不廢素業。

translations.literal: Though he passed through danger and ease in statecraft, he did not abandon his plain pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: Even through the perils of founding the state, he kept to his plain habits.

sentences.zh: 從諫察謀，以威重得衆。

translations.literal: He accepted remonstrance and examined counsel, and by stern weight won the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He heard remonstrance and weighed advice, and held the host by sober gravity.

sentences.zh: 卽位後，身不御精細之物，敕中書舍人桓景真曰：「主衣中似有玉介導，此制始自大明末，後泰始尤增其麗。

translations.literal: After he took the throne he would not himself use fine and delicate things. He charged Palace Attendant Huan Jingzhen: "In the wardrobe there seems to be a jade sword-girdle ornament; this fashion began late in the Daming era, and after Taishi it grew all the more lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he would not touch fine things himself. He told Palace Attendant Huan Jingzhen: "The wardrobe still holds a jade sword-fitting—fashion began late in Daming and grew worse under Taishi.

sentences.zh: 留此置主衣，政是興長疾源，可卽時打碎。

translations.literal: Keep this in the wardrobe and it will only breed long sickness at court—smash it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Leave it there and you nurse the court's sickness—break it now.

sentences.zh: 凡復有可異物，皆宜隨例也。

translations.literal: Whatever else is similarly out of the way should be handled by the same rule."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever else is extravagant should be treated the same."

sentences.zh: 」后宮器物欄檻以銅爲飾者，皆改用鐵，內殿施黃紗帳，宮人著紫皮履，華蓋除金花瓜，用鐵廻釘。

translations.literal: In the rear palace, utensils, rails, and balustrades ornamented with copper were all changed to iron; in the inner halls yellow gauze curtains were hung; palace women wore purple leather shoes; on the imperial canopy the golden melon flowers were removed and iron turning nails used instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the inner quarters copper fittings on rails and screens were switched to iron; yellow gauze curtains hung in the private halls; palace women wore purple leather shoes; golden melon ornaments were stripped from the imperial canopy and iron nails used instead.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「使我治天下十年，當使黃金與土同價。

translations.literal: He often said, "Give me ten years to rule All-under-Heaven and I would make gold the same price as earth."
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "Ten years on the throne and I would make gold worth no more than dirt."

sentences.zh: 」欲以身率天下，移變風俗。

translations.literal: He wished to lead All-under-Heaven by his person and shift custom.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to move the realm by example and change its habits.

sentences.zh: 上姓名骨體及期運曆數，竝遠應圖讖數十百條，歷代所未有，臣下撰錄，上抑而不宣，盛矣。

translations.literal: The emperor's name, bone and frame, and the dates and numbers of his destined fortune all far matched chart and prophecy in scores and hundreds of items such as no previous age had known; his ministers compiled them, but he suppressed them and would not have them proclaimed—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: His name, his frame, and the calendar of his fortune matched omen and prophecy in scores of ways no earlier reign had seen; ministers wrote them down, but he forbade their publication—magnificent restraint.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孫卿有言：「聖人之有天下，受之也，非取之也。

translations.literal: The court historian says: Master Sun has a saying: "When the sage possesses All-under-Heaven, he receives it—he does not seize it."
translations.idiomatic: The court historian writes: Xunzi said that when a sage holds the realm, he receives it—he does not take it by force.

sentences.zh: 」漢高神武駿聖，觀秦氏東游，蓋是雅多大言，非始自知天命；

translations.literal: Han Gaozu was divinely martial and sagely bright; when he watched the Qin emperor tour east, it was largely grand words in excess—he did not from the first know Heaven's mandate by himself;
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu was fierce and far-seeing; when he saw the First Emperor of Qin parade east, it was mostly swaggering talk—he did not yet know his mandate for himself;

sentences.zh: 光武聞少公之論讖，亦特一時之笑語；

translations.literal: Guangwu, when he heard Shaogong's prophetic talk, likewise took it at first only as a jest for the moment;
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu, hearing Shaogong's prophecy, likewise laughed it off at first;

sentences.zh: 魏武初起義兵，所期「征西」之墓；

translations.literal: Cao Cao, when he first raised the army of righteousness, looked only to the tomb marked "Campaign West";
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, when he first took up arms, aimed no higher than the grave that read "Campaign West";

sentences.zh: 晉宣不內迫曹爽，豈有定霸浮橋？

translations.literal: Jin Xuandi, had he not been pressed within by Cao Shuang, would he have fixed hegemony at the Floating Bridge?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi would never have seized power at the Floating Bridge had Cao Shuang not driven him to it.

sentences.zh: 宋氏崛起匹夫，兵由義立：咸皆一世推雄，卒開鼎祚。

translations.literal: The Song house rose from a common man; its armies were raised by righteousness: each in its time was pushed forward as the hero, and each in the end opened the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Song rose from the ranks; their armies were born of righteous cause: each age made its champion, and each at last won the throne.

sentences.zh: 宋氏正位八君，卜年五紀，四絕長嫡，三稱中興，內難邊虞，兵革世動。

translations.literal: The Song occupied the throne through eight rulers, divined for five reign-periods; four times the direct line died out, three times they called it a restoration; within, trouble; on the borders, alarm; war never rested.
translations.idiomatic: Song emperors reigned through eight rulers and five generations of omens; four times the main line failed, three times they hailed a "restoration"; at home rebellion, on the border raids, war without rest.

sentences.zh: 太祖基命之初，武功潛用，泰始開運，大拯時艱，龍德在田，見猜雲雨之迹。

translations.literal: At the beginning when the Grand Progenitor founded the mandate, military achievement was kept in reserve; when Taishi opened fortune, he greatly rescued the age's distress; dragon virtue in the fields—traces of suspicion like clouds and rain appeared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Progenitor first took the mandate, he kept his sword sheathed; in the Taishi years he dragged the age back from ruin; "dragon virtue in the fields"—yet already men read storm in his sky.

sentences.zh: 及蒼梧暴虐，釁結朝野，百姓懍懍，命懸朝夕。

translations.literal: When Cangwu grew tyrannical, grievance bound court and countryside; the people were fearful; lives hung by dawn and dusk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cangwu turned cruel, wrath filled court and field; common folk trembled, their lives measured from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 權道旣行，兼濟天下。

translations.literal: Once the expedient way was deployed, he aided All-under-Heaven together.
translations.idiomatic: When the time for hard measures came, he steadied the realm as well as his own house.

sentences.zh: 元功振主，利器難以假人，羣才戮力，實懷尺寸之望。

translations.literal: The supreme achievement shook the ruler; the sharp tool is hard to lend to others; the host of talents joined their strength, yet in truth they cherished hope only an inch wide.
translations.idiomatic: His merit outshone the throne; power is not lent lightly; the great men strained together, yet each nursed only a handbreadth of hope.

sentences.zh: 豈其天厭水行，固已人希木德。

translations.literal: Was it not that Heaven tired of the Water phase, and men already yearned for the Wood virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Had not Heaven wearied of Song's "water" mandate, and men already hungered for Qi's "wood"?

sentences.zh: 歸功與能，事極乎此。

translations.literal: To return achievement to the able and let affairs reach their limit—this was the furthest point.
translations.idiomatic: To give the merit to the man who could bear it and let the moment finish its course—that was the limit.

sentences.zh: 雖至公于四海，而運卽時來；

translations.literal: Though utmost fairness was shown to the four seas, the turn came with the time;
translations.idiomatic: Though he was just to the four seas, the hour itself pressed forward;

sentences.zh: 無心於黃屋，而道隨物變。

translations.literal: With no heart for the yellow house, yet the Way shifted as things changed.
translations.idiomatic: he had no lust for the throne, yet the Way moved when things moved.

sentences.zh: 應而不爲，此皇齊所以集大命也。

translations.literal: He responded yet did not act—therefore Great Qi gathered the great mandate here.
translations.idiomatic: He answered and did not grasp—and so Great Qi received the mandate.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：於皇太祖，有命自天，同度宇宙，合量山淵。

translations.literal: In praise: O august Grand Progenitor, mandate from Heaven; you matched the cosmos in measure, mountains and abyss in depth.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: O august Grand Progenitor, Heaven-sent; vast as heaven and earth, deep as mountain and gorge.

sentences.zh: 宋德不紹，神器虛傳。

translations.literal: Song virtue did not continue; the sacred vessel was passed in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Song's virtue failed; the sacred vessel passed empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 寧亂以武，黜暴資賢。

translations.literal: He stilled disorder by arms and deposed violence, relying on the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He stilled chaos with arms, cast down the cruel, and leaned on the worthy.

sentences.zh: 庸發西疆，功興北翰，偏師獨克，孤旅霆斷。

translations.literal: From the western marches he raised merit; on the northern frontier achievement rose; a detached column took the victory alone; a lone host cut like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: He stirred the west and built glory on the northern wall; one wing won alone; a single army struck like lightning.

sentences.zh: 援旆東夏，職司靜亂；

translations.literal: He raised his banner in eastern Xia and by office stilled rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: He raised his standard in the eastern lands and by his post quelled revolt;

sentences.zh: 指斧徐方，時惟伐叛；

translations.literal: He pointed his axe at Xu and the lands of the east—then was the time to punish traitors;
translations.idiomatic: he turned his axe to Xu and the east—the hour to punish rebels;

sentences.zh: 抗威京輦，坐清江漢。

translations.literal: He showed might at the capital and sat still while the Yangtze and Han were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: he showed force at the capital and, seated in silence, cleared the Yangtze and Han.

sentences.zh: 文藝在躬，芳塵淵塞。

translations.literal: Letters and arts were in his person; fragrant dust filled the deep frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Learning lived in his person; his fame filled even the far marches.

sentences.zh: 用下以才，鎮民以德。

translations.literal: He employed men by talent and settled the people by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He used men for ability and ruled the folk by virtue.

sentences.zh: 端己雄睟，君臨尊默。

translations.literal: He rectified himself with heroic gaze and faced the realm in honored silence.
translations.idiomatic: He straightened himself with a hero's eye and governed the realm in honored stillness.

sentences.zh: 苞括四海，大造家國。

translations.literal: He embraced the four seas and greatly made the house and state.
translations.idiomatic: He held the four seas and remade house and state.
